literal_quote.text: whether education will predict decreased conspiracy beliefs

findings.factual_answer: Both2017 and shipped2018 report the negative education association. Current abstract reports analyzing the same broad relation; an assertion that2018 is unrelated merely because its title concerns minorities would be false.

Explicitly attributed target is2017’s education mechanisms.2017 supports powerlessness/control and simple-solutions mediation in both samples, subjective class only Study1, self-esteem not supported, and serial analytic-thinking path inStudy2. Current abstract reports SES/cognitive reflection inStudy1 and powerlessness/scientific reasoning inStudy2. Scientific reasoning/curiosity are planned extensions; abstract alone cannot establish every final mediator test or original-mediator correspondence.

The recovered2018 original tests these comparisons in Dutch minority/majority samples. Neither available current abstract nor its matching preregistration establishes a current empirical retest of those comparisons. Missing current body prevents a definitive negative body-content claim.

Matching preregistration plans Slovak adult online samples. Current realized nationality, exact data-collection protocol, overlap between its two studies and any reuse cannot be certified from the missing final body. There is no affirmative evidence of reuse of the earlier Dutch data.

If the parent maps a shared negative education association,2018 also contains that empirical finding; distinct DOI/title alone cannot settle report equivalence or row treatment.
If the parent needs evidence that current tests2018-specific minority/deprivation findings, that is unestablished with present source completeness.

findings.relationship: Current OT–placebo direct emotional empathy to positive/negative MET scenes
findings.factual_answer: This is a concrete new within-subject behavioral comparison in35analyzed men,24IU; directly overlaps the direct-empathy component reported by Hurlemann2010 and Geng2018b. The2018b experiment also measures cognitive empathy and indirect arousal, uses a between-subject design and24/40IU in separate experiments. Current does not newly test sex generalization, cognition/arousal, learning, lesion or fMRI connectivity contrasts.

Current groups2018a with2018b in aim/confirmation citations, but primary2018a’s reported experiment measures empathic/self embarrassment to everyday embarrassing situations, with lower arousal/amygdala/insula responses. It cites its prior MET findings as2018b/reference10. The authors explicitly separate embarrassment-level ratings from feeling-intensity ratings and caution cognitive/emotional components are unresolved. A shared enhancement-of-ratings description does not establish the same empirical MET result.

Current expressly shares participants with Le2020(other tasks in same trial). Neither2018paper states that its participants or task data are reused from the other, and2018a’s Methods list no ancillary MET administration. Reported n70 versus72/69 and similar methods do not prove either independence or overlap across papers. No participant IDs or direct cross-paper mapping obtained; any unreported ancillary task remains unknown.

conditional_answers: If mapping the reported positive/negative direct-empathy treatment contrast, Geng2018b and Hurlemann2010 supply primary empirical antecedents.

If mapping specifically to2018a, the explicit bundled current citation supports author attribution but is not enough to establish retesting of2018a’s distinct embarrassment finding; parent must assess the codebook relationship using these distinct constructs/tasks.
If a report-equivalence claim depends on reused participants/data or an ancillary MET in2018a, additional primary evidence is needed.
limits: The current introductory48IU statement conflicts with2018b primary40IU; do not repair either source.
Reported indirect arousal increases in MET2018b and decreases in embarrassment2018a are distinct task findings, not interchangeable emotional-empathy measures.

findings.relationship: Differential behavioral sensitivity to suppression and estradiol/progesterone addback
findings.factual_answer: Current explicitly traces original finding/cohort1 to reference3, Schmidt1998; the2017Nguyen report also empirically documents symptom recurrence under the same broad hormone paradigm in its selected sample. Thus original attribution and existing-row report equivalence are separate questions, not decided by the absence of2017from the current target sentence.

2017tests steroid-metabolite processing after controlled addback: estradiol-3-sulfate and DHEAS change contrasts, no diagnosed-group difference in measured progesterone-derived neurosteroid changes. Current measures parent estradiol/progesterone plus clinical ratings; no corresponding metabolite assay/reanalysis identified.
